A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same LrcSSM research. All 21 pages of v4 and 20 pages of v5, including Appendices A–E, are readable and support comparison of text, equations, tables, and figures across their reorganization.

before.justification: v4 reports original LrcSSM classification results, PPG-DaLiA regression results, runtime measurements, nonlinear-model comparisons, and ablations in the main text and appendices.

after.justification: v5 retains these original empirical results, including the classification comparisons, PPG-DaLiA evaluation, runtime measurements, and Appendix E ablations.

M1.justification: The LrcSSM equations, diagonal state dependence, block architecture, Euler integration, and generalized recurrent-model constructions are retained. Algorithm 1 now presents the already discussed DEER/ELK methods with an optional quasi approximation; this clarifies existing solvers without establishing a new proposed procedure.

E1.justification: Both versions evaluate Heartbeat, SelfRegulationSCP1, SelfRegulationSCP2, EthanolConcentration, MotorImagery, EigenWorms, and PPG-DaLiA. Abbreviated dataset names in v5 do not change the classification and regression coverage.

E2.justification: Transformer and RFormer already appear in v4 Tables 1–3; v5 corrects the prose comparator count from nine to eleven. The corresponding PPG-DaLiA, MguSSM/GruSSM/LstmSSM, and ablation comparisons also retain their participants.

E3.justification: The validation-based hyperparameter search, selected configurations, evaluation metrics, and data-splitting protocol are retained. The nonlinear comparisons and ablations still use the fixed 64-dimensional encoding, six blocks, and 64 states; Euler integration with unit timestep and the 1000-training-step timing procedure also remain unchanged.

E4.justification: Appendix E retains the same capacitance, dense-versus-diagonal Jacobian, input/state dependence, and real-versus-complex parameter ablations. The preliminary integration-scheme observation and convergence-iteration analysis are also retained. Moving existing comparisons into the main text does not add an analysis.

E5.justification: The capacitance ablation's Average row changes from 63.4 and 65.4 in v4 Table 10 to 63.4 ± 7.8 and 65.4 ± 8.0 in v5 Table 8, adding uncertainty to previously bare averages. Existing five-seed reporting remains, with no stated increase in runs.

E6.justification: v5 Section 5.1 corrects the EthanolConcentration ranking statement from outperforming all methods to outperforming SSM methods. Both versions report LrcSSM at 36.9 ± 5.3 versus Transformer at 40.5 ± 6.3. Accuracy and MSE means, runtime values, and the remaining tabulated comparisons are retained.

T1.justification: Appendix A retains the contraction lemma, gradient-stability theorem, proofs, and scalability analysis. Appendix D retains the Euler reformulation and GRU derivation. Notation and explanatory edits do not introduce revised formal assumptions, bounds, or proofs.

C1.justification: The abstract, contribution list, and conclusion retain the same central claims: efficient parallel nonlinear recurrence through diagonal model design, gradient stability, preserved predictive capability, generalization to other recurrent models, and competitive benchmark performance. More general parallelization wording does not establish a new core contribution.

C2.justification: The explanations involving input correlations, biological mechanisms, LinOSS's ODE order and integration scheme, and diagonal-model expressivity remain substantively the same. The Newton-iteration overhead limitation is retained; its new Figure 2 reference points to an existing analysis.

D1.justification: v5 adds a code-repository access link on page 2 and identifies TU Wien dataLab and Liquid AI computational support in the acknowledgements. Appendix B's hardware, training-time ranges, hyperparameters, integration details, and dataset-access links remain unchanged.

R1.justification: v5 adds Lal et al. (2004) for MotorImagery and Vaswani et al. (2017) for Transformers. The broader research positioning is retained. Publication updates for Mamba, Liquid-S4, and LinOSS refer to existing cited works rather than new research coverage.

P1.justification: Generalization and ablation overviews move from Sections 3.2–3.3 to Sections 5.2–5.3, incorporating the former Appendix D.2 results discussion. v5 also standardizes dataset abbreviations, clarifies Algorithm 1 and parallelization terminology, and corrects wording and cross-references. Most prose and the overall narrative remain intact.

P2.justification: The main empirical displays are substantially reorganized: v4 Tables 1–3 become one compact table with six dataset columns and an average column, while appendix Table 9 becomes main-text Table 2. Appendix tables receive shorter labels and revised headers, and the runtime table and Figure 2 move beside Section B.5. Both figure graphics themselves are unchanged.

improvement.justification: The code-access disclosure, added aggregate uncertainty, and corrected Ethanol ranking improve reproducibility information and reporting accuracy. Bringing existing nonlinear comparisons into the main text makes supporting evidence easier to find, although the merged benchmark table uses smaller type. These are limited gains; the underlying experiments and formal arguments are retained.
